capacity_gross_kwh.notes: ArenaEV Model S 85: 85 kWh nominal, 350 V; EVSpecifications: 85 kWh, 346 V, 7,104 cells. Wikipedia: 85 kWh from 2012 Signature.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: No opened page states usable for the 85 kWh pack. Ratio 81.8 net / 85.8 gross = 0.953 on the Model X 90D page (same 7,104-cell Panasonic 18650 pack family, EVSpecifications lists 7,104 cells for both) x 85 = 81.0. Search-result snippets from EV Database/EVKX give 80.8 (pages not fetched: 429 / blocked). Basis is not same-cell: the 90 pack uses newer cells with the same 7,104 count.

chemistry.notes: EVSpecifications 2017-2018 Model S/X: NCA (Panasonic NCR18650A, LiNiCoAlO2); Wikipedia Model S: NCA cathode.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: Pack voltage 300-407 V (EVSpecifications: 302 V 75 kWh, 346 V 85/90 kWh, 400-407 V 100 kWh; ArenaEV 300-360 V), well below 800 V: 400 V class.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: a Model S owner's manual (ManualsLib page 145, undated edition, quoted: "When navigating to a Supercharger location, Model S may allocate energy to pre-heat the Battery"); Electrek (2020.24.6 release note) gives the same behaviour for Model S/X in 2020 software. No page says whether every MCU1-era car (2012-2017) runs it, and cars ordered without navigation (Tech Package; TMC thread 2019-03-07) probably do not. No manual battery control found. tesla.com manuals are 403.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EVSpecifications gives 120 kW for the 2014 85 kWh, 2015 85D, 2017 75D/90D and 2018 75D/100D/P100D Model S; carried to 2016 85 (other year or pack than the cited page). No page shows a pack-specific limit.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EVSpecifications 2017-2018 Model S (75D/90D/100D/P100D) list AC 11.5 kW (48 A); a 72 A / 16.5-17.3 kW higher-amperage charger was optional (EVSpecifications lists 17.28 kW on the 2018 Model X P100D). 2016 cars carried over from 2017; the pre-refresh 2016 cars (before about May 2016) may have the 10 kW single or dual charger.
